component.name: Apache Axis2/Java
component.description: SOAP and REST web services engine: a message-processing pipeline with pluggable transports (HTTP/HTTPS, JMS, TCP, local), a module system for cross-cutting concerns (WS-Security via Rampart, WS-Addressing), hot-deployment of service archives (AAR/MAR), and multi-protocol serving (JSON-RPC, REST/OpenAPI, MCP) from a single service deployment. Runs inside a Jakarta Servlet container (Tomcat, Jetty, WildFly) or embedded via Spring Boot.

externalReferences.comment: Source security threat model (SECURITY.md); this file is a structured translation of it.

blueprints.name: Axis2 message processing deployment
blueprints.description: Architecture described by the threat model: remote clients send untrusted input through the servlet container (TLS termination, optional authentication) to the AxisServlet/HTTPWorker HTTP entry point; a MessageContext is created and flows through transport-in handlers, dispatchers (URI, SOAPAction, WS-Addressing, JSON method, HTTP location), handler phases (where security modules like Rampart execute), message builders (SOAP, XML, JSON, MTOM, multipart/form-data), and the MessageReceiver that invokes the service method. Deployment happens by dropping AAR/MAR archives into WEB-INF directories on the filesystem.

assets.name: AxisServlet / HTTP entry point
assets.description: URL patterns exposed from the servlet mapping: /services/{ServiceName} (JSON-RPC and SOAP), /services/{ServiceName}/{Operation} (REST-style), ?wsdl and ?xsd metadata and /services/ listing (anonymous if exposeServiceMetadata=true, the default), and /openapi.json, /swagger-ui, /openapi-mcp.json when the OpenAPI module is engaged.

assets.name: Message processing pipeline
assets.description: Transport-in phase, dispatchers, global and per-service handler phases (security modules execute here), message builders, MessageReceiver, response phases and transport-out.

assets.name: Parsers and builders
assets.description: XML parsers (AXIOM/StAX, DocumentBuilderFactory), WSDL/XSD import resolution (wsdl4j, xmlschema-core), JSON parser (Gson), multipart/file upload (commons-fileupload2), MTOM/attachment handling, and context externalization via SafeObjectInputStream.

assets.name: Hot-deployment engine
assets.description: DeploymentEngine loading AAR/MAR archives from WEB-INF/services/ and WEB-INF/modules/. The trust boundary is filesystem access; there is no signature verification (deployment is an admin operation).

zones.name: Remote clients
zones.description: Anonymous clients (untrusted, no credentials, can reach any endpoint exposed by the HTTP transport, all input is hostile) and authenticated clients (partially trusted, identity verified by the servlet container, a servlet filter, or a WS-Security module).

zones.name: Axis2 engine
zones.description: The Axis2 framework running inside the servlet container: entry points, pipeline, parsers.

zones.name: Deployment filesystem
zones.description: WEB-INF/services/ and WEB-INF/modules/ directories written by trusted service deployers and module developers; deployed code executes with full JVM privileges.

persona.description: Fully trusted. Configures axis2.xml, deploys/removes modules and services, controls the servlet container. Has filesystem and JVM-level access.
Trusted. Drops AAR archives into WEB-INF/services/. May be the same person as the administrator, or a CI pipeline.
Trusted. Builds and deploys MAR module archives that add handlers to the processing pipeline. Code executes with full JVM privileges.
Partially trusted. A remote caller whose identity has been verified by the servlet container, a servlet filter, or a WS-Security module (Rampart). Authorized actions depend on the application.
Untrusted. A remote caller with no credentials; can reach any endpoint exposed by the HTTP transport. All input is hostile.

threats.name: Remote code execution via the Axis2 framework
threats.description: RCE through the Axis2 framework itself (not through user-written service logic) is a security issue. Historically the most severe class was deserialization of untrusted data; the removed Tribes-based clustering module exposed a network listener that deserialized Java objects from untrusted streams without validation, enabling RCE via standard gadget chains (AXIS2-6097). Any ObjectInputStream.readObject() on network input is a critical-severity finding.

threats.name: XML External Entity (XXE) injection
threats.description: The framework's XML parsers resolving external entities or allowing DOCTYPE declarations from untrusted input would enable file read, SSRF, or denial of service. CVE-2010-1632 was a DTD/XXE issue in the MTOMBuilder flow, fixed by strictly forbidding DOCTYPE declarations in SOAP and XML requests. Third-party XML libraries (wsdl4j 1.6.3, xmlschema-core) create their own parser factories that bypass framework-level hardening, so every XML parsing path, including transitive ones, must be audited.

threats.name: Server-side request forgery via framework features
threats.description: An attacker causing the server to make requests to arbitrary internal or external hosts through framework features such as WSDL/XSD import resolution, endpoint references, or transport senders, including file:// and gopher:// schemes in imports.

threats.name: Denial of service via parser abuse
threats.description: Billion-laughs XML bombs, deeply nested JSON, or other input causing unbounded memory or CPU consumption inside framework-level parsers, including large attachment DoS and temp file exhaustion in MTOM handling.

threats.name: Multipart/file upload abuse
threats.description: Unbounded file counts or sizes via multipart form data that exhaust server resources (the CVE-2023-24998 pattern in commons-fileupload 1.x).

threats.name: Authentication or authorization bypass in the handler pipeline
threats.description: A flaw in the handler/phase pipeline that allows a message to skip an engaged security module. Notably, a flaw in Axis2's handler pipeline that allows the Rampart module to be bypassed is a vulnerability in Axis2, even though flaws within Rampart itself belong to the Rampart project. Dispatch-level risks include routing to an unintended service, header spoofing, and JSON-RPC method name injection.

threats.name: Information disclosure of server internals
threats.description: Stack traces, class names, or configuration details leaked to unauthenticated callers through fault messages or metadata endpoints when exposure has been disabled.

threats.name: Path traversal
threats.description: A crafted service name, URI component, or WSDL import location that allows reading or writing files outside expected directories.

threats.name: Vulnerabilities in user-written services
threats.description: SQL injection, broken access control, or insecure business logic in a deployed service are the service author's responsibility, not Axis2 security issues.

threats.name: Missing authentication on endpoints
threats.description: Axis2 does not ship built-in authentication. Securing endpoints is the responsibility of the servlet container, servlet filters, or engaged security modules (Rampart).

threats.name: Arbitrary code deployment via weak filesystem permissions
threats.description: If an attacker has write access to WEB-INF/services/ or WEB-INF/modules/, they can deploy arbitrary code via a malicious AAR/MAR. The trust boundary is filesystem access; this is an OS/container configuration issue, not an Axis2 vulnerability.

threats.name: Service enumeration via /services/ listing and metadata endpoints
threats.description: When exposeServiceMetadata is true (the default), service names, WSDL, and XML Schema are visible to anonymous callers. This is documented behavior controllable via axis2.xml.

threats.name: Denial of service at the network level
threats.description: SYN floods, slowloris, or transport-layer attacks are mitigated by the servlet container, not Axis2.

threats.name: Vulnerabilities within optional, external modules
threats.description: A flaw in Rampart's cryptographic implementation would be handled by the Rampart project. However, a flaw in Axis2's handler pipeline that allows the Rampart module to be bypassed is a vulnerability in Axis2. Dependency-level CVEs are historically the most frequent class (admin console CSRF/XSS CVE-2010-3981, HttpClient CVE-2012-6153/CVE-2014-3577, commons-fileupload CVE-2016-1000031 and CVE-2023-24998).

threats.name: Use of unencrypted, unauthenticated raw transports
threats.description: The TCP transport uses raw sockets with no encryption or authentication, and UDP has no encryption, authentication, or reliability; both are for trusted networks only. JMS authentication is delegated to the JMS broker, mail transport depends on mail server authentication, and HTTP TLS is handled by the servlet container.

trustBoundaries.name: HTTP entry trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: Remote client input passes through the servlet container (TLS termination, optional authentication) into the AxisServlet and message processing pipeline; anonymous client input is hostile.

trustBoundaries.name: Deployment trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: AAR/MAR archives dropped into WEB-INF directories execute with full JVM privileges; the trust boundary is filesystem access and there is no signature verification.

controls.name: Hardened XML parser factories
controls.description: All DocumentBuilderFactory and SAXParserFactory instances created by the framework disable DTDs and external entities (XMLUtils.java, SecureWSDLLocator.java, DefaultEntityResolver.java); DOCTYPE is disallowed and DefaultEntityResolver returns an empty source.

controls.name: SecureWSDLLocator for WSDL imports
controls.description: SecureWSDLLocator pre-validates imported documents with a hardened SAX parser before passing them to wsdl4j, rejects DOCTYPE, protocol-whitelists to HTTP/HTTPS only, enforces a size limit (10MB default) and connect/read timeouts, and blocks the relative-path SSRF bypass.

controls.name: Hardened schema import URI resolvers
controls.description: URI resolvers for AAR and WAR deployments block HTTP/HTTPS/FTP/JAR/file scheme resolution to prevent SSRF via xmlschema-core's DefaultURIResolver.

controls.name: SafeObjectInputStream deserialization whitelist
controls.description: The remaining use of Java serialization (context externalization) goes through the whitelist-based SafeObjectInputStream, restricted to known Axis2 context classes.

controls.name: Clustering module removed
controls.description: The entire Tribes-based clustering module (inter-node communication with unvalidated deserialization enabling RCE) has been removed from the codebase in 40+ files (AXIS2-6097).

controls.name: commons-fileupload2 file count limits
controls.description: Migration from commons-fileupload 1.x to commons-fileupload2 in 2.0.0 (driven by CVE-2023-24998) enforces file count limits, preventing unbounded-file-count DoS. MTOM/attachment handling uses streaming processing with TempFileManager cleanup.

controls.name: Dispatcher and method name validation
controls.description: Dispatchers validate service existence and unknown services return a fault; JSON-RPC method names are validated against deployed operations and unknown methods return a fault. The optional ?fields= query parameter validates field names against the declared response type with no dynamic class loading.

controls.name: Fault detail suppression
controls.description: sendStacktraceDetailsWithFaults defaults to false, keeping stack traces out of fault messages.

controls.name: Fuzz testing of parsers
controls.description: Jazzer-based fuzzers cover XML, JSON, HTTP header, and URL parsers, with 45M+ iterations and zero crashes or security findings; the JSON parser has 1.7M+ iterations with Gson nesting limits. Axis2/C has an active OSS-Fuzz integration.

controls.name: Authenticate endpoints at the container or module level
controls.description: Secure endpoints via the servlet container, servlet filters, or engaged security modules (Rampart); Axis2 ships no built-in authentication.

controls.name: Protect hot-deployment directories
controls.description: Restrict filesystem write access to WEB-INF/services/ and WEB-INF/modules/, since anyone who can write there can deploy arbitrary code.

controls.name: Control metadata exposure via exposeServiceMetadata
controls.description: Service listing, WSDL, and schema disclosure are controllable via the exposeServiceMetadata parameter in axis2.xml (default true).

controls.name: Restrict raw TCP/UDP transports to trusted networks
controls.description: The TCP and UDP transports provide no encryption or authentication and are for trusted networks only.
